persistence_invariants.brief: Each (sku, location) pair is uniquely addressable; no two records share that pair. A collision is resolved at write time (R3).
Stock quantity never goes below zero; a pick that would overcommit is rejected at write time (R2).
Existing stock data survives every schema migration with no loss; each additive model change preserves inventory records created before it (R1).
Every inventory adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor; these audit fields are NOT NULL and immutable on update (R1).

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every schema migration with no loss. Each iteration's additive model change preserves the inventory records created before it, and every inventory adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor.

Stock levels never go below zero, and never overcommit beyond available quantity. A pick that would overcommit is rejected at write time (never a stored negative, never a silently-allowed double-allocation).
Every SKU at every location is uniquely addressable by (sku, location) and no two records share that pair. A collision is resolved at write time (never two stored duplicates, never an error page).

Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch databricks_postgres database, not a mock or in-memory substitute. The CI workflow refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.

The UI is a single-page web application. The warehouse-floor tablet loads the app once and navigates client-side (home, SKU detail, receipt/pick/adjustment forms) with no full-page reloads. A stock adjustment updates the affected row in place (optimistic update, reconciled against server response) rather than re-rendering the page. The client is a React + TypeScript application under client/, and the backend is a JSON API (boundary returns data, not server-rendered HTML).
